In other words, is it automatic whenever there's a joint action - and "joint," using in a non-military sense, just togetherness - between the MUP and the VRS? That's the first thing, isn't it? You're saying it's effectively automatic because of, as you put it, the principle of singleness of command.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. The next issue on that is how the MUP comes to be in a resubordinated position. In other words, does it come about without a request; or does there have to be a request? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we discussed both cases. The case in which a commander decides on his own, based on assessment of the situation, to resubordinate all of the forces, including the civilian authorities, to his command. We've also discussed cases in which a commander talks to the Ministry of the Interior, the public security station, seeking to have certain forces allocated to him for a particular mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, as I say, that's one of the other issues. The third is, what is the status of police officers who are in a resubordinated position in the military? In other words, are they military conscripts, as you suggest, and therefore lose all their rights and entitlements as policemen; or do they remain policemen who are merely acting under the orders of the army? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I said there needs to be a document that deals with this. A resubordination document or a document on a unit being dispatched somewhere. For example, a police unit is sent off to become a part of a military unit. Its members temporarily lose their status as the officials that they are. For the duration of that particular mission, they become military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that's what you're saying, and I'm going to ask you on what possible basis you make that assertion when we get to it. Fourth issue, really, is: Who was responsible for carrying out or taking disciplinary proceedings and/or criminal proceedings during a period when a police officer, or police officers, were subordinated, resubordinated to a military command? And as I understand your assertion, it is that the military would be responsible for the taking of disciplinary action and criminal proceedings. Am I correct in understanding that's what you say?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, that would be the authority of that unit's commander. All members of that unit are subject to rules and regulations, or, rather, the unit commander must initiate proceedings against individuals found to have committed some disciplinary infraction or, indeed, criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. So that all depends on whether you are correct in your assertion that police officers resubordinated effectively are members of the military. They are conscripts. Because if they're not, then - would you agree? - disciplinary and/or criminal, depending on the nature of the offence, whether it's a military offence or a civilian-type offence, would be the responsibility of the police officer's chain of command. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You insist that for resubordination, for the police to become members of a military unit or command, there has to be a document. I mean, that's a precursor, is it, to any proper resubordination?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, that's what the theory says. It is in that document that many individual things, rights and commitments, depend, anything at all that stems from that document which also regulates all of that when the resubordination commences, as well as when it ends. Other things mentioned are also the different costs, travel costs, various types of expenditure. So in one word, yes. There needs be to a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if there isn't a document, if no one has produced a document saying, The Banja Luka - no, let's take a small one - the Prnjavor, your brother's station, SJB is hereby ordered to supply 20 men for the purposes of combat - because it has to be combat, doesn't it? - to the army, and no document is produced to that effect, a military commander rings up -- rings up - gets in touch with the SJB chief, says, I need 20 men, send them over right away. And the SJB chief does that. And nobody ever produces a document about that. It's all unofficial. Well, then, that is an illegal action by both the SJB chief and the army officer. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, when I spoke about document, it's is quite possible that orders are verbally transmitted, as you showed us yesterday. And a verbally transmitted order is then recorded in a log-book. Reference is included in the duty officer's reports. If this unit is off on a combat mission, in my opinion there needs to be an underlying document. It is a serious activity. Sending men to battle is a serious activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, quite. But it's not just battle you're talking about, apparently. And you've said -- I'm sorry, you've said over and over again, There has to be a document, because all sorts of things are regulated by that document, not just the length of the service, but the payment and all the rest of it. So let's go back to what I was saying. If no such document is brought into existence whatsoever, is that not, in your book, an illegal action? It's contrary to the regulations and the law.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, it is not illegal. According to the rules and regulations, a superior officer may issue a verbal order by which he commands and conveys orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But supposing - and just looking at it this way - the -- the SJ -- the commander who's got in touch with the SJB Prnjavor doesn't want police officers to fight, to engage in combat, as defined. He simply wants the police to, if you like, stick up a roadblock to make sure that people fleeing from the village don't get away. Are you saying then that the police unit that does that is resubordinated to the military?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we need to analyse this on a case-by-case basis, in view of the mission and the contents and the purpose of sending a unit. If this police force and this barricade, roadblock, is within the zone of responsibility of a certain commander, then these elements of the police force are resubordinated and placed under the command of this particular commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, if you take that to its logical conclusion, General, then, if police officers acting in the zone of responsibility of a brigade commander commit a serious crime, such as the killing of over 100 people, it is the brigade commander who is responsible for the criminal investigation of those police officers and the disciplining or otherwise, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Ms. Korner. If, at that time, they were subordinated to him and took part in a joint operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, that's not what you said before. What you said a minute ago was: "If the [sic] police force and this [sic] barricade ... is within the zone of responsibility of a certain commander, then ... elements of the police force are resubordinated and placed under the command of this particular commander." So, therefore, if what is happening is that police officers, for example, are transferring prisoners and commit offences, it's not the responsibility of the police to investigate. It's the responsibility of the army. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that this is either mistranslation or -- I don't want to confuse the witness. But I would like to hear from the witness. Since he understands a little English, I don't want to suggest any -- anything to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What Ms. Korner is saying, that the witness didn't say, is not something that is -- that derives from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can I start this and then I think it's time -- probably time for the break. But can I just put this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If, in this example, the commander, the brigade commander, says to the SJB, "I want you to lend me -- or your part in this is to set up a roadblock and prevent people from fleeing from the village which I'm about to shell with my troops," and during the course of that activity, when the roadblock is set up, the police who are manning it kill the fleeing civilians or catch them and beat them, it is your contention, is it, that it is the military who are responsible for investigating the crime?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner. Provided these men were subordinated to this commander within the task performed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... but, you see, we keep going round in endless, ever-decreasing circles. And the reality is, isn't it, that resubordination was done, as it's properly understood, was done on rare occasions for effectively large-scale military operations, such as Operation Corridor?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, in my report I stated and asserted that when the police was used for combat, there always has to be resubordination. And you can only have one commander. You are giving me various examples, and I don't know what is the particular status of this unit in the events that you are describing. But I know that the commander of the brigade, of the corps -- or the corps must know what is going on, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And all of this, as you say, this resubordination, depends on there being a document to that effect, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either a document or a decision of the commander in charge, which confirms that he has engaged a number of men and subordinated them to himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... I thought that was -- I'm being told it is time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It is actually. We're past the time. But there was a question put to you, General, by Ms. Korner, regarding the authority to investigate and possibly either prosecute or initiate disciplinary proceedings against anyone who, while being resubordinated from the police to the army, commits a crime. And I don't think you answered that part of her question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said, and I stand by it, that for as long as police officers are subordinated to a military commander it is up to the military commander to undertake all possible measures, including disciplinary and criminal actions, against individuals who are committing infringement of discipline or violate the rules of international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so we'll take a break and return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: General, as we already established, you had no personal experience of the combat or, indeed, the events in Bosnia after May of 1992. That's correct, isn't it? No personal experience.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what you are claiming, Ms. Korner. I did not take part in any combat activities after May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not claiming anything, General. I thought you -- that's what you told us. In Bosnia, in 1992, you took no part in the military activities, nor, at that stage, were you a member of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, the term "military activities" is a rather broad notion, but I do accept what you say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Nor, in fact, have you ever personally had resubordinated to you, or asked for the resubordination in the course of your military duties, of police?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to ask if you'll agree with these statements. If a brigade commander wanted to request resubordination, as a commander, he had to do it through regular or interim combat reports to his superior commander.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, a commander, in compliance with the prevailing situation on the ground, may take such a decision, either independently, or independently but he is obliged to inform, about this decision, his superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. So you wouldn't agree that before he could ask for the police to resubordinate men he had to get the permission of his commander?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in keeping with the current situation. And tomorrow, I'm going to show you the article of the law which says that a battalion commander can independently decide to employ certain forces and include them in his unit that, for example, have to perform some work obligation or other type of obligation that stems from mobilization that was declared in a country or in a certain region.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Would you accept this: That the request made by the brigade commander had to include a statement of reasons, whether -- that a -- for example, that a situation had occurred that demanded such resubordination; and it would be the superior who would decide whether the request was granted within the superior's own framework of competencies?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in every single case, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, as a general rule, then, would you agree that that statement is correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that a battalion commander may request the draft office that keeps the records of all conscripts, to have even the chief of the public security station be sent to him. And then, subsequently, he is duty-bound to inform the superior who is at the next level above him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. That -- just answer, please, the question I ask. I really do have limited time. As a general rule, would you agree that the statement that a situation that -- the brigade commander had to include a statement of reasons to his superior, and it was his superior who would decide whether the request was granted. As a general rule, would you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, Ms. Korner, that that is how it was supposed to be. But I would like to underline that according to the law it is possible for a commander to act independently.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you're going to tell me what law that is tomorrow, so let's just carry on with this. Would you also agree with this statement: If, during a period of resubordination, a civilian police officer commits a disciplinary offence, the chain of command who would deal with it would be that of the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Ms. Korner. I keep saying that if a person is subordinated to a military commander, then it is the military commander who undertakes certain measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So if any brigade commander thought that was the position, he was totally and utterly wrong; is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in general, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I mean specifically. If a brigade commander was under the impression -- not the impression - was sure that if the disciplinary offence were to be committed by a resubordinated police officer it would be the police officer's own chain of command that would deal with it. That's wrong, according to you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the rules in force, I think that he would be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you don't think. You've been asserting throughout this that he is wrong.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you agree that, even when resubordinated, the police officers were under the command of a police -- the ordinary police officers were under the command of a superior police officer who, in turn, would be under the command of a military officer?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you agree that, even where there was resubordination, the police commander would be reporting on the events, and the like, to his immediate superior in the police?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, this police commander is subordinated to a military commander, and it is to him that he is reporting about all the activities and all the details pertaining to his unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, as far as you're concerned there would be no circumstances in which a police officer in charge of a resubordinated unit would be sending reports back, about what was happening, to his superior officer in the police?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I already said that if he is subordinated to a commander of a military unit, the chain of reporting is identical to the chain of command for the duration of this situation and until such time as this policeman is returned to his police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Just before we look at the documents: On what law do you base your assertion that when a police officer is resubordinated under the terms of Article 104 he loses all rights and responsibilities as a police officer and, ergo, does not report to his superior officer? Under what law? Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, this is contained in all the military rules that govern command relation, the principle of singleness of command and subordination. The law provides that if a police unit is resubordinated to a military unit, it becomes subordinated to the commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. It says "resubordinated." But where does it say - leaving aside singleness of command - where does it say a police officer resubordinated is no longer a police officer and therefore has no rights of payment, pension, responsibilities, such and such; where does it actually say that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I think that this is provided by Article 11 of the Law on Mandatory Military Service. It defines the moment when someone becomes a member of the unit, and it stipulates the status thereafter that he acquires and all the entitlements that he is granted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But that has nothing to do -- that has to do, does it not -- not that we've got that law, as far as I know - that has nothing do with the -- the borrowing, if you like, of some police officers and resubordinating for the purpose of combat?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we mentioned the Law on All People's Defence several times so far, and this is where this is very clearly stipulated and provided.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it doesn't say anything of the sort, does it? I don't want to have up for the nth time Article 104. It says "for the purposes --"

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I suppose we better have it up. Can we have up document 104. L1, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Actually, I don't want to go -- because I am short of time and we've seen it a number of times and it's a matter of interpretation. You interpret it one way, and we suggest that, on the evidence, you're wrong. So can we look, please, now, first of all, at one of the documents you were shown by the Defence, which is P603, and it's document 95 in the Defence bundle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, that's not the one I want to have a look at.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, that's definitely not the one I want. Yes. It's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now I would ask you, General, to keep your answers really, really short from now on because there are a lot of documents that I want to show you. This is the order to the command of the 10th Partisan Division on 1st of April, 1992. As you pointed out when you were asked about it, this is still the time of the JNA and you do not know the circumstances of this order. "Establish full co-operation," well, it's co-ordination, although I think the translation still says co-operation, "...with the organs of government in Sanski Most municipality and collaboration with TO --" well, let's have a look at the exact words. Sorry, does it say -- I'm sorry, perhaps you should read it out. Read out that part, would you? Under order: 1; the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I quote: "Implement a full co-operation with the authorities in Sanski Most municipality and co-ordinated action with the TO and police units."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now, and you say that means that the officer to whom this order was given, in fact, as we know, Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic, was resubordinating the police and TO to his command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, as I've already said several times, if it's about co-ordination or co-ordinated action with TO or police units, then any of the forces being co-ordinated in the implementation of that task are subordinated to that commander. In addition to that, we don't have a co-ordination plan here. We don't see the specific forces involved. We don't see the specific police units involved. Therefore, it's highly imprecise, from my perspective.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And you don't know what was happening in Sanski Most at the time, do you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, Ms. Korner. You keep taking me back to a specific event, and what I'm talking about is the theory, the rules, and the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know. But we've been through this a number of times. The theory is all very well, but the practice, you would accept, wouldn't you, General, may be very different?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I agree with you. I have addressed the issue too. I know what war means, and it doesn't always work based on theory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the one person who could have addressed what he understood by this order and what happened is the person to whom it went, Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may just add this. This is a slightly different situation than we would encounter with an ordinary witness. The present witness is an expert who may well have been in a position to obtain confidential material or even documents under seal. He took up this commitment when he was scheduled to appear. He knows and has signed a document to that effect that he is under no circumstances allowed to disclose any of the material used in the process of drafting his report. So the situation is slightly different. The present expert -- the present witness, being an expert witness, is allowed to access certain types of confidential material and has already assumed the responsibility and undertaken the obligation of keeping this to himself and under no conditions disclosing any of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. But, of course, the -- that's -- that's -- what happened today is a slightly -- is a variation on that principle, so the injunction by the Court is nevertheless necessary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we move on, please, General, to a document you've also been asked about before, which is the 15th of May MUP order from Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's document 1D46. Tab 17. Well, no it's been twice actually. Tab 16 or tab 17A.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is the order from the MUP side, which, I take it, you had not seen until you got here. You didn't see it before you drafted your report.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Ms. Korner, this order was discussed during my examination by Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. No. What I'm -- sorry, I think you misunderstand. You didn't see it. It's not part of your bibliography; let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now, what Mico Stanisic is doing here, you spent a long time with Mr. Cvijetic over the theory that there were two police forces being set up by this order. One that was being resubordinated, and another that remained as police officers. But in item number 3, it states: "Due to difficulties existing in communication lines with the Security Services Centre, I hereby authorise chiefs of the CSB to organise the authorised officials of the ministry in the [sic] territory ... in the war time ..." So the chief of the CSB has to get authority from his own chief; namely, the minister of the interior? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then can we go to item 7, which is -- yes, next page in both.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is what I was asking you about earlier, about authority from above: "The use of the ministry units in co-ordinated action with the armed forces ... may be ordered by the minister of the interior, the commander of the police detachment of the ministry (for the Sarajevo ...) and the chief of the CSB ... for the territory of the [sic] jurisdiction." Do you agree that the use of the word "may" means that it is not a given that police forces will be used; it is within the authority of the minister or the chiefs of the CSBs?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, as far as I understand, these are some preliminary actions and activities being undertaken by the ministry to establish, organise, and train its own units during a mobilization, if already implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. It says -- it doesn't talk about during mobilization at all. It says: "The use of the ministry units in co-ordinated action with the armed forces," which is what we've been discussing. "The commander of the police detachment and chiefs of the CSB shall inform the ministry of any use of the units," and there we have the repetition of paragraph Article 104, "whilst participating in combat operations the units of the ministry shall be subordinated to the command of the armed forces." So we're talking about, aren't we, the MUP side of these co-ordinated actions, resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner. I see that paragraph now, which confirms what are you say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And can we go back to my original question, which is that: What is being said there by the minister is "may." It's not a given that they will be used. It depends on the authority of him or his chiefs of the CSBs.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, it reads here that the Ministry of Interior "may" order this, that the commander of the police detachment and the commander of the ministry branch covering, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... yes --

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, that doesn't imply any use being made when a unit is subordinate -- resubordinated. So this person may decide that a unit will be on its way somewhere as soon as a request is received from one of the relevant officers. The minister provides instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. General, I mean, we're making this really complicated. All I'm saying is it's clear, isn't it, from this document, that what is being said is, it is up to the minister, or the chiefs of the CSB, to decide whether or not to order an attachment to the army?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, as far as I remember, the Law on Defence states that it is the president of the republic that decides on the use of the police in war time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've already -- but we've been through that, and you went through it with the Defence, I think. You agree that the minister -- the president of the republic delegates certain powers to the minister of the interior in the same way as he delegates them to the Chief of the Main Staff? I thought that's what you told us a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I'm afraid I have not been following closely enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You said only --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see Mr. Cvijetic on his feet, but I'm afraid I'm not prepared to take any objections from Mr. Cvijetic. It's enough that we have Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Ms. Korner please quote exactly what the witness said, instead of summarizing the witness's answers. Could she please provide a specific quote, transcript page and, as I said, exactly what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I won't because I haven't got time, and I'm going to be asking for further time as a result of all these footling objections that are going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, but, I'm sorry, but we're entitled to reference, Your Honours. We're entitled to reference. If Ms. Korner is putting something to the witness, then she must give us a reference to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm putting it as a result of his reply. I haven't got the reference here, but I will look it up if I'm coming back to this. I would like to move on from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do I understand that you do not agree that this document shows plainly that the minister and the chiefs of the CSB have the right to refuse a request from the military?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if you look at the command system, especially in war time, each order must be carried out, unless it runs counter to the rules and regulations applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But what I'm putting to you is that the person who wants the use of police as a resubordinated unit has to put or should put in a request. That's what this order from the minister means. Now, do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that these are not military terms being used. However, these are no military officers. And that is why the term may, here, be interpreted in this way. In the military, there is no such word as "may," no modality. There are orders being given by a person to another person, addressing specific tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But you accept that clearly the minister was under the impression that he or his chiefs had the right to refuse, by the use of the word "may"?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, it's what we've been talking about. I find the definition of the following paragraph much clearer and more precise. It talks about combat operations being carried out. The units of the ministry are resubordinated to the command of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Please, please just answer the question I ask. I'm glad you find the next paragraph clearer. Does it seem that the minister thought that he had the right to the -- refuse?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I -- I can't reply in terms of deciding what the minister may have meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... no, I agree. Only the minister could tell us what he meant. But to anybody reading it ... all right. Let's move on. We'll see what his subordinates thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, at P376. Tab 26.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 28th of May, so some ten days or so, maybe a fortnight, after Mico Stanisic's order. Stojan Zupljanin is sending to all SJBs and the corps command and the chief of the corps security, and this is the Prijedor Police Station copy, it looks like. He talks about the armed conflicts, the security situation, and so on. [As read] "With regard to this matter and bearing in mind that further uncontrolled activity could have major undesirable consequences, et cetera, all armed action and police activity is hereby forbidden without a prior decision and the consent of this CSB and the relevant corps command of the armed forces of the Serbian republic. Therefore, SJB chiefs and other responsible SJ [sic] officials cannot order the police to take armed action, particular to go to the areas of others SJBs to carry out certain missions, activities, without the prior consent of the CSB and the relevant corps command." Would you agree that Stojan Zupljanin is saying that my consent, as the chief, is needed before any SJB police officers can go off and carry out, -- I suppose, combat actions with the military?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Now, going back to what I was asking you about originally. What he's complaining about is SJB chiefs and other SJB officials are apparently sending off the police [indiscernible] armed action without the consent of the relevant corps authority or his. In those circumstances, would those actions be illegal?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if the commanders on the ground directly took that unit and resubordinated it to themselves, I assert to you that they had every right to do that. Nevertheless, the centre chief, or the commander of that station, should have reported to his superior about that before going out on a mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you've -- I thought you told us that nobody below the level of a brigade commander could order the police to be resubordinated. I thought you told us that at least half a dozen times.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, the battalion commander, as I specified, is the lowest level.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But, clearly, what's going on here is something completely different, according to the complaint. So let's say somebody below the level of a battalion commander is taking these SJBs off. That would be, would that not be, on your definition, illegal, subject to disciplinary proceedings on both sides at the very least?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, as I said, the law states that the battalion commander is the lowest level which, in extraordinary circumstances, may decide to take someone and resubordinate that someone to himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So, in fact, it can go to any level, according to you. Can we move, then, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm truly sorry. The comment: "So, in fact, it can go to any level, according to you." The witness, for the nth time, said the battalion commander is the lowest level. I'm not sure I understand the comment by Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I'd rather carry on. And we'll forget -- can we scrub that comment? If we were in the States, we'd say "strike it." Can we move, please, to the -- sorry. Yes, to the 6th of June. And that's P1794.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could we have a tab number, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is what's been called Directive 1. It's a directive of the Main Staff of the 6th of June. Or, rather, the Mladic, I think. Have you ever seen that before? No, it's not in your bibliography. Have you ever seen it before in any other circumstances, whether at conferences, analyses, whatever?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is exactly what I'm thinking about, and thank you for your assistance. I can't quite remember. It's possible, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. What it deals with is the various operations, in particular, Operation Corridor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at the third page in English and the second page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the second stage, says this directive, in a duration of four to six days create a corridor between Semberija and Bosnian Krajina and reject the enemy forces away from the communications. Then 5: Tasks of the unit: The 1st Krajina Corps from OG Doboj uses its main forces to defend the attained lines, and so on and so forth. Then: By persistent and active defence, and in concert with the 2nd Krajina Corps, maintain the attained front line, use appropriate grouping of forces and - this is all translated as - co-action with the East Bosnia Corps to break the enemy forces. Now, I can't see, but is the word used in both cases "sadejstvo [phoen]," or whatever it is?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the Supreme Commander -- oh, not Supreme Commander. I'm sorry. The Chief of the General Staff is ordering two completely different corps to act together in the -- for the purposes of this operation, using that word. Would you agree with that? Three corps, in fact.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we see how that was translated by the 1st Krajina Corps into action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At number 33, please -- sorry. Document 33 is P1 -- yes, 1795.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is Colonel Ludvig Krajnc on behalf of the 1st Krajina Corps, who, on the 10th of June, is sending out the operation to -- sending out the order, and how its going to carry out its task, to the various units involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, at the next page in B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Distributed to, you see, we see the list of subordinated units. And on the next page as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Or is it the same? No, I think [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, this is a receipt. So these units received it. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you also agree that for an operation of this size, this order would have to go to all the units who were expecting to take part, all subordinated units expecting to take part, in this operation?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we haven't seen the entire document. But as a rule, the contents of a document have to be conveyed either to all units or only those subordinate units that are taking part in a specific mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now let's look, please, at page 2 in English, and page -- sorry, not page 2. It's - one, two, three, four - page 5 in English, and I believe it's the same in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Paragraph 2: Task of the 1st Krajina Corps. Second paragraph: Task: Using persistent and active defence, and in co-ordination with the 2nd Krajina Corps, hold the current front line. And by grouping the forces advantageously and in co-ordination with the East Bosnia Corps defeat enemy forces. And the word is the usual word. Now, it's right, isn't it, that the commander of the first --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, but I think this is, again, a translation error, because the word, what you said, "co-ordination," it's "sadejstvo." "Co-ordination." "Action."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I know. Oh, sorry. Co-ord-- yes, I'm so sorry. Yes, I meant to say it's "sadejstvo" again, in each case, "co-ordinated action." Now, it's right, isn't it, that the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps cannot order by use of the word "co-ordinated action" either the 2nd Krajina Corps or the East Bosnia Corps?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner. A corps commander only commands his units in line with the task assigned, the plan, or whatever he receives from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And therefore the use of the word "co-ordinated action" in this context does not mean that the 2nd Krajina Corps or the East Bosnia Corps are, in fact, subordinated to the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I understand why you are asking me this. Along with this directive, as I mentioned earlier, a co-ordination plan has to be worked out, and then plan of co-ordinated actions, in which it is designated which forces from a corps will be part of the command or subordinated to the operation commander. In this case, the commander of the Main Staff is ordering both corps to make these forces available that have been provided in the plan of co-ordinated action. And then, again, they have to be subordinated to the operation commander who is entitled to use elements of the 1st, the 2nd, and the 3rd Krajina Corps, or any other forces placed at his disposal for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I perfectly understand that. What I'm trying to establish, as you understand, is that the use of the word "co-ordinated action" does not automatically mean that the unit or the persons that are being discussed are, in fact, subordinated. And I think you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is said that all the three corps commanders are subordinated to the commander of the Main Staff. And they must not do anything without a decision of the Main Staff commander regarding this particular operation. The commander of the Main Staff, either authorised them, or gives them an order, with relation to which forces are going to be involved. It does not mean that the entire corps are going to be involved in this operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I -- I understand that. I perfectly accept that. That the Main Staff is ordering these three corps, who are subordinate to them, to carry out this operation. But General Talic or his -- Colonel Kranjc sending this out is not suggested by, the use of the word "co-ordinated action," that the other 2nd Corps are co-ordinated [sic] to him. Is that right? Can you just say yes or no, please, because we've got about five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they're not subordinated in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. The -- the 1st Krajina Corps then goes on to list under paragraph 5 the tasks of the units which are subordinated to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can we come, please, to 10, paragraph 10 of this document, which is - one, two, three, four, eight, nine - page 10, I think, yes. Thank you. Under (b), security support: Focus of security support in all units and safe-guarding the commander's decisions, and so on and so forth. "In all units, a part of the forces are to be ready to defeat and destroy infiltrated sabotage and terrorist groups and other enemy special forces in co-ordinate --" I suppose it says co-ordinated action. I can't see the ... well, whatever it says. "... in co-ordination with neighbouring forces and police forces on the ground." Now, is it your contention that when he is using that phrase, and I can't find it at the moment in B/C/S, but I assume it's the usual phrase of co-ordinated action, yes, I can see it is, finally, General --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if you're reading the second paragraph under (b), I don't think that that shows to the -- to the General on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. All right. Can we ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you see that paragraph I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is it your contention that General Talic is, here, resubordinating, by the terms of this order, the police forces for the purposes of this Operation Corridor?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, one cannot conclude that from this portion of the order. I'm telling you that there must be a commander of the operation and there must be forces taking part in the operation. These forces have to be put together under a single command. He is going to take decisions himself with relation to all the forces that he received from other sources, whether it's logistics or any other tasks, as part of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's all that I'm trying to establish, that the use of the word "co-ordinated action" does not automatically imply resubordination. And, indeed, we went through the distribution list, and no CSB, SJB, or anybody appears on -- any MUP unit appears, does it, on that distribution list?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, you put me two or three -- put two or three questions to me. As far as I can remember, there were no public security centres who received this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, then that -- that will be an appropriate moment for today. Your Honour, however, as I say, I have lost, over the last few days, a great deal of time that I've asked for through objections and arguments about the admission of documents. Your Honours said yesterday that I had until -- only until the end of the first session tomorrow. Your Honour, I would ask for a little more time because I still have to deal with a number of other issues in this case. I don't know how long Mr. Krgovic intends to re-examine for, but it may well be that he, in fact, wouldn't finish his re-examination tomorrow in any event. But I'm asking that I may have a little extra time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, first of all, I think that this request of Ms. Korner is not justified. Ms. Korner spent a lot of time of her examination dealing with marginal issues. Only one session yesterday and today dealt with some of the crucial matters and the issues that are contained in the expert report and his -- the appearance of the expert witness here. My intention was to conclude my re-direct examination as soon as possible in order to allow the witness to leave on the Friday. I'm afraid that with this request of Ms. Korner this is not going to be possible. Of course, it's not up to me to suggest to the other party how they should conduct their examination, but, as I said, I think that Ms. Korner dedicated at least three days only to the introductory part of the report, without going into any key issues, and I think that was her problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, how long -- how long do you think you will have for -- need for re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that I need two or three sessions for re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The last -- the last information you gave us was one session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was two days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. So -- so it increases by one session a day. Then let's finish this as quick as possible then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Anyway, we will make this determination tomorrow. But I remind counsel that whereas we appreciate that it is up to counsels how to conduct his or her case, our responsibility is in terms of management of the trial. And one of the realities that we are hard up against is to avoid any witness being -- waiting here for two weeks. We must complete such witness as is called next week by the time we rise on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has determined that this witness will be released tomorrow. And to that end, the -- by the time we reconvene tomorrow morning, the Court Officer would be in a position to report as to whether it is possible to have an extra sitting from 2.30 to 3.30/4.00 tomorrow afternoon. Working back from that towards the morning, we would expect Ms. Korner to complete her cross -- we would require Ms. Korner to complete her cross-examination by the third of the second session tomorrow. So that's an extra 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So we rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
